answer: Make each identity prove it lives somewhere for 30 days. First, the device signs a daily GPS and Wi-Fi fingerprint, an ember of routine lit in one place. Second, the network checks all 30 prints form one coherent route, not leaps across a canyon. Third, any gap restarts the 30-day clock before it can earn. Fourth, peers audit 5 percent of routes. Faking 1,000 identities means running 1,000 phones in 1,000 real places for a month, about 90,000 dollars in devices and data, plus 30,000 device-days. A sonnet needs fourteen lines in order; an identity needs thirty days in one place.
